claims.claim: Rio Tinto's copper, aluminium and lithium diversification links electrification and infrastructure demand to a broader critical-material supply base rather than a single iron-ore exposure; AP60 commissioning provides present capacity-conversion evidence.
The Winu consent framework strengthens the project-to-resource bridge, while final economics, schedule and commodity prices remain explicit conditions rather than assumed outcomes.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Copper, aluminium and lithium are infrastructure/electrification inputs and already contribute more than half of disclosed underlying EBITDA.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Commodity diversification reduces single-commodity dependence, but major-project economics and commodity cycles remain material.

factors.name: supplyChainResilience
factors.basis: AP60 adds aluminium capacity and Winu could broaden copper supply, but Winu is not yet an operating asset.

risks.risk: Successor bottlenecks can shift from resource availability to permitting, social license, project execution, power and commodity economics.

causalEdges.mechanism: grid, transport and industrial systems require conductive and battery materials
causalEdges.falsifier: material intensity falls faster than end-demand grows or substitutes structurally displace these inputs

causalEdges.from: Rio diversified production and AP60/Winu capacity pathway
causalEdges.mechanism: existing diversified earnings plus commissioned/proposed capacity can relieve material constraints
causalEdges.falsifier: project delays, consent loss, poor economics or commodity oversupply prevent durable economic supply

unknowns.unknown: Winu final economics and development timing remain unestablished.

claims.claim: Present diversification and productivity evidence is real, but does not remove commodity-cycle, capital-intensity or major-project execution exposure.
Winu's consent milestone improves social-license evidence but should not be inflated into proof of final project economics or schedule certainty.

factors.name: commodityCycle
factors.basis: Cash generation remains sensitive to commodity prices despite diversification.

factors.name: confidenceInflation
factors.basis: Commissioning and consent milestones are concrete; extrapolation to full ramp and project returns remains prospective.

risks.risk: Commodity-price weakness or cost inflation can offset productivity and capacity gains.
Large projects can consume capital before economic output is proven.

causalEdges.mechanism: realized prices, costs and ramp timing determine whether physical capacity becomes economic value
causalEdges.falsifier: diversified volumes and productivity sustain returns through adverse commodity scenarios

contradictions.claim: Strong current diversification versus persistent commodity cyclicality
contradictions.resolution: Diversification reduces concentration but does not eliminate shared macro/commodity exposure.

unknowns.unknown: Full AP60 ramp and Winu investment returns remain future checkpoints.
